text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Giant Cell Arteritis (Temporal Arteritis)

Despite the normal ESR and visual field tests, your age, new onset headache, and progressive vision loss are highly suspicious for Giant Cell Arteritis. The lack of systemic symptoms like fever or weight loss does not rule this out. I will proceed with a diagnosis based on this clinical picture, but typically we would confirm with a temporal artery biopsy and check for elevated inflammatory markers again if they were not definitively excluded. Given your history of hypertension and high cholesterol, these are common comorbidities but do not explain the acute vision loss and headache as well as GCA would. If you were to undergo a temporal artery biopsy, it would likely show granulomatous inflammation. The normal visual field test is concerning but can occur early in the disease or if the ischemia has already occurred. I recommend immediate high-dose corticosteroids to prevent permanent blindness.
